Our position is that the customer-side indemnity stays narrow while the vendor indemnity covers IP infringement without a knowledge cut-back.

ops.oldText: (iii) to the best of its knowledge the Creative placed onto Customer's platforms or websites by the Auction Platform;

proposal.summary: Narrow Customer indemnity to Content/Properties and breach of Law; remove knowledge qualifier from Kubient's Creative indemnity.

quote: (iii) Customer's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement, or (iv) the Content or Properties, including any allegation or claim that the Content or Properties violate or infringe on an y third party rig hts, or (v) the acts or omissions of Customer or a third party hired by, employed, retained or under Customer's control.
rationale: Section 10(a) does contain a Kubient indemnity covering the Services, the Auction Platform and Kubient's breach of its warranties (which include the IP ownership warranties at 9(b)(vii)-(viii)), and Section 11 sets out standard notice/control/cooperation procedures, so the vendor-side limb of the rule is largely met. Two deviations remain: (1) our indemnity in 10(b) is far broader than the playbook's narrow position, extending to breach of any representation or warranty and to an open-ended catch-all for the acts or omissions of Customer or anyone under its control; and (2) Kubient's indemnity for Creative served through its own Auction Platform is cut back by a "to the best of its knowledge" qualifier, weakening cover for third-party IP and content claims arising from demand Kubient controls. The redline narrows our indemnity to the Content/Properties and our breach of applicable Law and deletes the knowledge qualifier.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no ownership provision, so we have added one confirming that AP retains all rights in its Content, Properties and Request/user data, that Kubient assigns any deliverables it creates for us (with a licence back to any embedded Kubient IP), and that Kubient receives only a limited service-delivery licence in Customer Data with no joint ownership. Kubient keeps the Auction Platform and its pre-existing tools, so this simply confirms the parties' expected positions; if Kubient prefers, we can accept a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to deliverables instead of assignment.

ops.text: (b) Ownership of Content, Customer Data and Deliverables. As between the Parties, Customer owns and retains all right, title and interest, including all intellectual property rights, in and to the Content, the Properties, the Inventory, the Requests, and all data and materials provided or made available by Customer or collected from the Content, the Properties or Customer's users in connection with the Services (collectively, "Customer Data"). Kubient owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Auction Platform and its other pre-existing technology, tools and know-how, together with any general improvements thereto. Kubient hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to any deliverables, reports, analyses or other work product created for Customer under this Agreement (excluding Kubient's pre-existing technology), and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense any Kubient intellectual property embedded in such deliverables for Customer's business purposes. Kubient is granted only a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use Customer Data during the Term solely as necessary to provide the Services, and no right, title or interest in Customer Data or Customer's other intellectual property is assigned or transferred to Kubient. Nothing in this Agreement creates joint ownership of any intellectual property.

proposal.summary: Add IP and Customer Data ownership clause: AP owns Content/Properties/data and deliverables; Kubient keeps platform; limited licence only, no joint ownership.

quote: Customer shall be responsible and solely liable for all the Content (including without limitation all intellectual property rights therein) and the Properties.
rationale: The Agreement contains no intellectual property or data ownership article. Section 6(a) (p0025) only allocates liability for the Content and Properties to AP, and § 14(b) (p0065) addresses names, trademarks and logos only. Section 2 licenses the Auction Platform to AP, but nothing confirms AP's ownership of its Content, Properties, Inventory, Requests or visitor/user data (which Kubient collects, measures and stores per § 9(b)(iii)), and nothing addresses ownership of, or a licence back to, deliverables Kubient creates for AP. No clause affirmatively assigns AP IP or data to Kubient (so this is not a walk-away), but the silence leaves AP short of the preferred position that we own what we pay for and everything we put in. Added one ownership subsection: AP owns Content/Properties/Customer Data; Kubient retains the Auction Platform and pre-existing tools; Kubient assigns deliverables with a perpetual royalty-free licence to embedded Kubient IP; Kubient receives only a limited service-delivery licence in Customer Data; no joint ownership.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] This Agreement excludes consequential damages but contains no monetary cap, so both Parties are exposed without limit. We have added a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of twelve (12) months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 (a fee-only basis would be illusory under the revenue-share model in Section 5), with indemnification, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sitting outside the cap. We can accept a mutual cap of twelve months' amounts with carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

ops.text: (b) Except with respect to Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable between the Parties under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights; and amounts owed by a Party under Section 5 shall not be treated as damages subject to this Section 7(b).

proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap (greater of 12 months' amounts and USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims to Section 7.

rationale: Section 7 contains only a mutual exclusion of consequential/indirect damages (p0027), carved out for indemnification and confidentiality. A document-wide search for "aggregate", "exceed" and liability language returns no monetary cap anywhere, including in the warranty (Section 9) and indemnity (Sections 10-11) provisions. Both parties are therefore exposed to unlimited direct liability, which fails the rule's requirement of a mutual cap at a meaningful amount. A fees-based cap alone would be illusory here because Section 5 is a revenue share under which Customer pays Kubient no fees, so the redline uses amounts paid or payable between the Parties with a USD 1,000,000 floor, and places confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
rationale: Section (h) is a mutual assignment clause with a consent standard that is expressly "not to be unreasonably withheld," plus a consent-free carve-out allowing AP to assign to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all of its relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation — the core preferred protection for the Customer. A document-wide search for "change of control" returns no results, and the termination provisions contain no Kubient right to terminate or re-price on an AP change of control (only mutual insolvency/breach triggers at p0016), so no walk-away trigger is present. The only gap versus the preferred position is the absence of an express bar on Kubient assigning to an AP competitor; given the clause is otherwise symmetric and balanced (and satisfies the fallback of mutual successor assignment with a reasonableness consent standard), reopening it to make the carve-out one-sided is disproportionate. Note the Kubient License at p0002 is stated to be "non-transferable, non-assignable," but that limits sublicensing/transfer of the license grant itself rather than assignment of the Agreement, which is governed by (h).

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: Section 1 (Kubient Services) expressly negates exclusivity and confirms that AP remains free to offer Inventory through other agents or sell to third parties, which matches our preferred position of no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on the Customer. The only other "exclusive" references are a non-exclusive license grant to us (p0002), exclusive jurisdiction (p0064), each Party's ownership of its own marks (p0065), the entire-agreement clause (p0072) and a no-third-party-beneficiary clause (p0073) — none of which restrict our procurement freedom. Searches for requirements/preferred-supplier, non-compete and "Customer shall not" restrictions returned nothing relevant.

quote: Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination fee payable by AP, so the preferred position (no Customer-payable LD) is already met. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "shall pay" and "minimum" returned no Customer-payable stipulated-sum remedy, and a full read of all 75 paragraphs confirms none. The only money-on-termination provision, § 4(a), entitles Kubient to "all fees generated during the termination period" — under the § 5 revenue-share model Kubient collects from Advertisers and remits AP's share, so this is Kubient's share of revenue actually earned during the 90-day notice period rather than a pre-estimated sum payable by AP; it is also expressly disapplied where AP terminates for Kubient's material breach. The Initial Term lock-in in § 4(a) carries no associated fee. § 7 excludes punitive damages mutually, § 14(d) prevailing-party fee recovery is reciprocal and not an LD, and § 13 disclaims any minimum revenue guarantee for either Party. AP's only payment obligations are taxes (§ 5) and its indemnity (§ 10(b)), neither of which is a liquidated amount. No redline required.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Auction Platform licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (who operate our ad stack), removed the at-will "revocable" and "non-assignable" wording so the licence ends only on expiration or termination under paragraph 4, and confirmed it transfers with a permitted assignment under paragraph 14(h). If helpful, we can accept affiliate coverage on written notice to Kubient as a fallback.

ops.newText: Kubient hereby grants to Customer and its affiliates, and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf, a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive license (transferable to a successor in connection with a permitted assignment under paragraph 14(h), and sublicensable to such affiliates and contractors solely for Customer's benefit) to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient, which license shall not be revocable except upon expiration or termination of this Agreement in accordance with paragraph 4,
ops.oldText: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,

proposal.summary: Extend Kubient licence to AP affiliates and contractors, remove at-will revocability, and permit transfer to a successor.

quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,
rationale: The grant in paragraph 2 runs to "Customer" only, with no coverage for AP affiliates or the contractors that operate our ad stack, and is expressly "revocable" as well as non-transferable, non-assignable and without sublicense rights. A bare "revocable" licence lets Kubient pull platform access at will outside any termination event (paragraph 4 / 14(h) contemplate termination and permitted assignment to affiliates and successors, but the licence itself would not follow). The redline adds affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, limits revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4, and makes the licence transferable with a permitted assignment under paragraph 14(h), aligning the grant with the assignment clause the parties already agreed.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: The agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant binding the Customer, so the preferred position is met. Searches for "compet*", "exclusiv*", "restrict", "solicit", "similar/field of use/territory" and negative-covenant phrasings ("Customer will/shall not", "agrees not to") returned no restrictive covenant on our business. To the contrary, p0001 affirmatively disclaims any exclusive arrangement and expressly preserves AP's right to offer or sell Inventory through other agents or to third parties — language that benefits us and should be retained. The only "Customer will not" language, in p0025 (Use of Service), is ordinary license-scope and IP protection (no transfer or third-party access, no derivative works, no reverse engineering, no resale or service-bureau use of Kubient's Service). Those limits govern how we may use Kubient's own technology; they do not restrict the businesses AP may operate or the products AP may buy, build or license from others, so they are not a field-of-use restriction under this rule. The general survival provision in p0070 carries forward no such covenant because none exists. No redline is required.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a customer right to terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' notice with a pro-rata refund of any prepaid fees, and limited Kubient's convenience right to the end of the then-current term on ninety (90) days' notice, since as drafted we are locked in for the Initial Term while Kubient may walk away after it. We also removed Kubient's entitlement to all fees generated during the notice period so that termination carries no penalty; if helpful, we can accept 60 days' notice instead of 30.

Kubient may not terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term or any renewal term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit, and may terminate this Agreement for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer. Each Party shall remain entitled to its share of revenue generated during the notice period in accordance with paragraph 5 and the applicable Exhibit, and no early-termination fee or other penalty shall be payable by Customer in connection with any termination,

Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,

proposal.summary: Add AP convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; limit Kubient's convenience right to end of term; remove fee forfeiture on termination

quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
rationale: Paragraph 4(a) gives AP no convenience right at all during the Initial Term (a 12-month lock-in on an agreement that auto-renews indefinitely), while granting Kubient a symmetrical for-any-reason right after the Initial Term exercisable at any time on 90 days' notice — the reverse of the playbook allocation. It also strips AP of its revenue share by giving Kubient all fees generated during the notice period, functioning as an early-termination penalty. Redline adds a 30-day AP convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, confines Kubient's convenience right to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice, and removes the fee forfeiture; fallback of 60 days' notice offered in the comment.

quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification, or records-examination right exercisable by Kubient against AP. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verify" return no hits, and a full read of the single section confirms the point: the fees provision (p0023) is a pure revenue-share with sequential liability and imposes no obligation on AP to open books or systems for verification, and no compliance or use-of-service provision (p0024-p0025) grants Kubient examination rights. The only access obligation binding AP is in p0001, which is limited to "access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services" — that is forward-looking delivery cooperation tied to performance, not a verification or audit right, and it carries no inspection, frequency, cost, or system-access consequence. Because there is no audit right binding our party, the AUDIT walk-away risks (unlimited/unannounced audits or remote access to AP systems) are absent and the preferred position's frequency, notice, independent-auditor, cost-shifting and no-system-access limits have nothing to attach to. Adding audit machinery here would only create an audit right that does not currently exist, which is worse for AP than silence, so no redline is proposed. (Separately, note that Impressions are "measured by Kubient" under p0009 with no AP verification right — a customer-favorable audit right over Kubient would be a distinct ask outside this rule's scope.)

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the governing law from Delaware to New York so that the substantive law matches the agreed exclusive New York, New York forum; our position is New York law with the state and federal courts in New York County. If Delaware law is important to you, we can accept Delaware law and Delaware courts instead, but we would then need Section 8 conformed so disputes go to the courts rather than mandatory arbitration.

ops.newText: laws of the State of New York
ops.oldText: laws of the State of Delaware

proposal.summary: Change governing law from Delaware to New York to match the New York County forum

quote: (a) This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of Delaware without giving effect to its conflict of laws principles. Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York, New York.
rationale: Section 14(a) selects Delaware law but a New York, New York exclusive forum. Delaware law is only an acceptable fallback and the playbook fallback pairs Delaware law with Delaware courts; the preferred position (New York law with the state and federal courts in New York County) is reached with a one-word change to the jurisdiction words, leaving the agreed forum intact. Venue is court-based rather than foreign arbitration, so no walk-away issue arises, although Section 8's mandatory AAA arbitration (no foreign seat specified) conflicts with the exclusive court jurisdiction and is flagged in the comment for conforming.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or best-terms provision in either direction. Searches for "most favoured/favored", "no less favourable", "favorable" and "best terms" returned no hits, and the only commercial terms provision (§5 Fees and Payment, p0023) simply defers revenue-share economics to the applicable Exhibits without any obligation on AP to match or extend terms given to third parties. Section 1 (p0001) affirmatively confirms the arrangement is non-exclusive and does not restrict AP from offering Inventory via other agents or selling to third parties, which is directionally favourable to us. Consistent with the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), no redline is required. If a fees Exhibit is later added, MFN or best-terms language running against AP should be checked at that point.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: The agreement imposes no minimum purchase, minimum spend, take-or-pay or shortfall obligation on AP. The economics are a pure revenue share on actual auction activity (§5, p0023: "The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement... as set forth and detailed in each applicable Exhibit"), so AP pays nothing absent usage; the only Customer payment obligation is applicable taxes. Section 1 (p0001) expressly disclaims exclusivity and confirms AP may offer or sell Inventory through other agents or third parties, so there are no volume caps or channel restrictions on AP. The two "minimum" hits are benign: p0014 defines Winning Bid Price by reference to AP's own agreed floor price (a protection for us), and p0062 is a disclaimer that no minimum revenue is guaranteed (not a commitment by AP). The Initial Term lock-in in §4(a) restricts termination but does not create any purchase or volume commitment, so it falls outside this rule. Commercial Exhibits are not exposed in this document; if an Exhibit introduces a minimum spend or volume commitment, we would revisit under the fallback (commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up).
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: The relationship of the Parties is that of independent contractors, and nothing herein is intended, nor should be construed, to create a partnership, agency, joint venture or employment relationship.
rationale: Searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce" and "recruit" across the single-section agreement return no restrictive covenant on hiring or soliciting personnel; the only employment-related language is the independent-contractor provision (p0066), indemnity references to persons "hired by, employed, retained" (p0051, p0052) and confidentiality handling by employees (p0056, p0061). No non-solicitation or no-hire obligation binds the Customer (AP), which is the playbook's preferred position, so no edit is required.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We shortened the notice needed to exit an automatic renewal from 90 to 30 days, asked Kubient to remind us 60 days before each renewal, and capped any renewal-term pricing change at the lesser of CPI and 3%, consistent with our position that renewals be easy to exit and predictably priced. As a fallback we can live with a 60-day notice window and a 5% cap.

ops.newText: Either Party may terminate this Agreement, or elect not to renew the Term, for any reason following the Initial Term upon thirty (30) days written notice to the other Party. Kubient shall notify Customer in writing at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current Term of the upcoming automatic renewal. Any increase in fees payable by Customer, or reduction in Customer's revenue share, applicable to a renewal term shall not exceed the lesser of (i) the increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%).
ops.oldText: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.

proposal.summary: Shorten post-Initial Term exit notice to 30 days, add Kubient renewal reminder 60 days before renewal, and cap renewal pricing changes at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

quote: This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
rationale: Section 4(a) provides indefinite automatic 1-year renewals, but the only exit is a 90-day written notice — three times our preferred 30-day window and beyond even the 60-day fallback, sitting at the walk-away boundary. There is also no Kubient reminder before renewal and no cap on renewal pricing (fees/revenue share are set by Exhibit and could be reset at renewal). The redline keeps the 12-month renewal term, cuts the non-renewal/convenience notice to 30 days, adds a 60-day renewal reminder from Kubient, and caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 60-day/5% fallback available.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4(c) only addresses cessation of the Services and Confidential Information, so we have added a standard exit clause requiring Kubient to provide up to six (6) months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and certify deletion thereafter. If six months is not workable, we can accept ninety (90) days of transition assistance with the same 30-day data return.

ops.text: (v) upon Customer's request, Kubient shall provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at Kubient's then-current rates; within thirty (30) days of such request, Kubient shall return to Customer all Content, Requests, reports and other data of or relating to Customer or the Properties then in Kubient's possession or control (collectively, "Customer Data") in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and thereafter Kubient shall delete all Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and data return/deletion obligation in Section 4(c)

rationale: Section 4(c) is the sole effect-of-termination provision and addresses only cessation of the Services, revocation of the licence, Customer's ceasing use, and return/destruction of Confidential Information. There is no obligation for Kubient to provide transition assistance or to return AP's data (Content, Requests, visitor data collected and stored by Kubient under Section 8(iii)/p0035) in a usable format, nor any deletion/certification timing. In a hosted auction-platform services arrangement this absence is a deviation from the playbook, so we insert a new Section 4(c)(v) requiring up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter (fallback: 90 days' assistance with the same 30-day export).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Kubient's warranties in Section 9(b) have no conformance-to-specification commitment and no stated remedy, so we have added a 90-day conformance warranty and the standard re-performance, repair/replacement or refund remedy. Our position is that the vendor must stand behind its work with a real remedy; we can discuss making the refund the fallback only where re-performance is not practicable.

ops.text: (xii) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Service and each deliverable provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to the applicable specifications and documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 9(b) is, at Kubient's option, prompt re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Service or deliverable.

proposal.summary: Add conformance-to-specification warranty period and repair/replace/refund remedy to Kubient's warranties

quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
rationale: Section 9(b) contains most of the preferred warranty content — performance to industry standards (p0034), services free from material errors (p0038), no malicious code (p0036), compliance with Laws (p0041) — and the Section 13 disclaimer expressly carves out "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so the "as is" language does not swallow the express warranties. However, there is no conformance-to-specification/documentation warranty and no warranty remedy anywhere in the Agreement (no "refund", "re-performance" or "sole remedy" language appears), leaving us without the repair/replace/refund entitlement the playbook requires. We inserted a 90-day conformance warranty plus the standard re-performance, repair/replacement or refund remedy as new Section 9(b)(xii); the existing warranties run for the Term, which already meets or exceeds the preferred duration.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no insurance covenant, so we have added a short one in General Provisions requiring commercial general liability (USD 1M/2M), professional liability/E&O (USD 2M), cyber and privacy liability (USD 5M) and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request. Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and, per Section 9(b)(iii), collects and stores visitor data, so cyber cover is essential to give the indemnities in Section 10 real financial backing; if helpful we can accept E&O of USD 1,000,000 and cyber of USD 2,000,000 as a fallback.

ops.text: (j) Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: (i) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (ii) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (iii) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000, covering Kubient's collection, maintenance, management and storage of visitor information (data) and Customer's Confidential Information; and (iv) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law. Each policy shall be placed with insurers of recognized financial responsibility. Kubient shall name Customer as an additional insured on the commercial general liability policy to the extent of Kubient's indemnification obligations hereunder, and shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp) as new General Provisions subsection (j).

quote: (i) This Agreement is intended for the sole and exclusive benefit of the Parties hereto, is not intended to confer any rights or benefits on any third party, and only the Parties may enforce such Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement has no insurance clause: a full-text search for "insurance" returned no hits, and a read of all 75 paragraphs confirms General Provisions (Section 14, p0063-p0073) runs from governing law through counterparts with no insurance covenant. Kubient is a hosting/services vendor that operates the Auction Platform and, under Section 9(b)(iii) (p0035), "collect[s], maintain[s], manage[s] and stor[es] ... visitor information (data)" — i.e. it processes our data, which is the trigger for cyber cover under the rule and squarely outside the walk-away position. It also gives broad indemnities in Section 10(a) (p0047-p0051) covering the Services, the Auction Platform and third-party Creative, which are unsupported by any insurance backstop, particularly given the mutual consequential-damages waiver in Section 7(a) (p0027). Inserted a single new subsection (j) after p0073 in the existing General Provisions section — the smallest edit reaching the preferred position — requiring CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M, cyber/privacy of USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, additional-insured status on the CGL policy, and certificates on request. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M offered in the comment.
